title: Preregistered study: generate–verify–repair vs LLM-only and templated automation for NetOps change correctness
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair pipeline (LLM generation + deterministic network verifier + automated repair loop) produce fewer unsafe network changes than (a) LLM-only generation and (b) templated automation on a standardized NetOps change workload?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline yields a lower unsafe-change rate (fraction of intents whose final accepted change fails verifier checks) than the LLM-only pipeline, assessed as a paired difference in success rate (GVR minus LLM-only).
H2: The GVR pipeline yields a lower unsafe-change rate than the templated-automation pipeline for the non-templateable (complex-intent) subset.
H3: Median repair iterations per intent under GVR ≤ 2 (exploratory confirmatory summary) and repair iterations correlate negatively with final success probability.
exploratory_questions: E1: How prompt-template and seed variation affect unsafe-change rates (prompt-sensitivity ablation).
E2: Latency and model-call overhead trade-offs per avoided unsafe change.
E3: Distribution of failure severities (reachability vs policy) across pipelines.
benchmark_scope: synthetic_topologies_v1 (10 topology profiles: datacenter, small-enterprise, campus, small-isp variants)
intent_spec_v1 (intent grammar used to synthesize tasks)
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (difference in per-intent safe-change success probability: GVR - baseline)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N_confirmatory = 500 distinct intents (same set run under all three pipelines in paired fashion). Intent mix: 60% templateable (300 intents), 40% complex (200 intents). Topology clustering: 10 topology profiles; intents stratified evenly across profiles (50 intents per profile). Exploratory ablation: 100-intent held-out subsample (20% of N) for prompt-seed sensitivity. Randomization: fixed deterministic sampling seed frozen in preregistration for reproducibility.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute paired increase of 0.08 (8 percentage points). Two-sided family alpha = 0.05 with Bonferroni correction for two confirmatory tests => per-test alpha = 0.025. With N=500 paired intents and plausible within-pair discordance (~40%), approximate power > 0.8 to detect ~7–9 percentage-point absolute paired differences. Sensitivity analyses pre-registered for baseline success rates (0.6–0.8) and discordance (20–60%).
missingness_plan: Technical failures (API/network/infra) are logged and classified. Primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary': exclude intent pairs without complete final-accepted-change outcomes for both GVR and comparator. Pre-registered sensitivity: treat technical-failure pairs as unsafe ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). Missingness reasons enumerated in execution manifest and included in final report.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by registered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 using estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline' (GVR minus LLM-only). Per-intent outcome binary = success (final accepted change passes deterministic verifier) vs unsafe (fails). Pairing is by intent across pipelines. Primary treatment of technical failure = 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat failed-generation pairs as unsafe). Report 95% bootstrap CIs for paired difference and two-sided exact paired-proportion tests (McNemar or exact as appropriate). Subgroup analyses: templateable vs complex intents, per-topology-profile. Exploratory analyses (prompt/seed ablation, latency) labeled exploratory.
multiplicity_plan: Two confirmatory comparisons pre-specified: (1) GVR vs LLM-only (primary), (2) GVR vs templated on complex intents (secondary). Bonferroni correction applied across the two confirmatory tests (family alpha = 0.05 => per-test alpha = 0.025). Other comparisons reported as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Benchmark names: synthetic_topologies_v1, synthetic_device_configs_v1. Risk factors: model API nondeterminism, prompt leakage/overlap between training data and synthetic tasks, prompt-injection style adversarial inputs, verifier modeling abstraction errors. Detection: deterministic input-output hashing to detect duplicates/leaks; ensemble verifier consistency checks to flag disagreements; synthetic adversarial-augmentation held-out tests. Item-flagging rules: flag parser failures, primary/secondary verifier disagreements, generated changes containing anonymization placeholders. Analysis treatment: primary verifier is adjudicator for main result; pre-registered sensitivity uses conservative consensus (if either verifier fails => fail). All flagged-item counts and outcomes reported.
stopping_rule: Complete execution for all required_confirmatory_task_count = 500 paired intents. Early termination only for documented unrecoverable infrastructure failure; such stoppages logged and treated per missingness_plan, with sensitivity analyses reported.
planned_outputs: IEEE CNSM short paper (five-page) reporting preregistration, methods, results, and disclosure
raw experiment artifacts (inputs, model outputs, verifier logs, anonymized configs)
analysis result files (paired outcomes, bootstrap CIs, test statistics)
